candidate.title: TruSeq Targeted RNA Expression
candidate.scope: The single linear TruSeq Targeted RNA Expression library-preparation schematic in the assigned Illumina poster footer, from total RNA through cDNA, custom-oligo hybridization, extension-ligation and indexed amplification to a cluster-ready DNA library. No alternative method or version is depicted. This is schematic-level architecture, not a complete experimental implementation or a sequencing/analysis workflow.

states.label: Total RNA containing the biological target
features: The target is highlighted in yellow within a longer RNA line; the drawing represents a target region rather than a complete transcript inventory.

evidence.locator: Top material: Total RNA; yellow segment labeled Target between purple flanks

states.label: cDNA containing the RNA-derived target region
features: Blue strand with a yellow target segment, produced from total RNA before target-specific oligos are added.
cDNA is the hybridization and extension template; the biological analyte remains RNA expression.

evidence.locator: Unlabeled downward arrow from Total RNA to blue/yellow strand labeled cDNA
Total RNA to cDNA arrow
evidence.rationale: The named RNA input and cDNA output imply synthesis of complementary DNA from the RNA template; the diagram does not identify the reverse-transcription reagents or priming scheme.

states.label: Custom ULSO and DLSO oligos
features: Pink ULSO at left and green DLSO at right have bent outward tails.
The gap-facing end of DLSO is labeled 5′ P, identifying a 5′ phosphate at the ligation interface.
The two oligos are reagents for one target-templated reaction, not separate alternative workflows.

states.label: ULSO and DLSO hybridized to the cDNA target flanks

evidence.locator: Hybridization: separated pink and green arms lie along the cDNA on opposite sides of its yellow target segment; DLSO retains the 5′ P label

states.label: Continuous target-spanning oligo product paired with cDNA

The original blue/yellow cDNA remains drawn as the lower template strand.
Target information is now represented in an amplifiable DNA product with oligo-derived flanks.

evidence.locator: Extension-Ligation: continuous upper pink/yellow/green strand paired with lower blue/yellow cDNA
Hybridization to Extension-Ligation: the upper gap becomes a continuous yellow segment joining pink and green arms
evidence.rationale: The cDNA target segment is yellow before and after the reaction; a matching upper yellow segment appears under Extension-Ligation, joining the pink ULSO and green DLSO arms. The gap-facing DLSO end is labeled 5′ P before joining. Together these support cDNA-templated extension and a ligation interface at the phosphorylated DLSO end, without specifying enzymes.

states.label: Amplification primers bearing P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 sequences
features: The left primer tail is labeled P5 and Index 2; the right primer tail is labeled Index 1 and P7.
These labels describe terminal adapter/index components used at amplification, not additional biological targets.

evidence.locator: Denature and amplify: separated target-spanning strands with P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 primer extensions; arrow to terminal duplex
Denature and amplify and terminal library bearing P5, Index 2, Target, Index 1, P7
evidence.rationale: The amplification-stage primer tails and the same labeled segments in the final duplex support incorporation of the terminal adapters and indexes during amplification; exact PCR chemistry and read layout are not specified.

states.label: Indexed target-containing DNA library ready for cluster generation
features: Final duplex has the left-to-right labeled organization P5, Index 2, Target, Index 1, P7, with intervening colored oligo-derived segments.

The central region is explicitly labeled Target; it is blue in the endpoint drawing, whereas the target was yellow in the preceding stages. The shared label and connected route establish its target association without treating colors as chemical formulas.
Index 2 and Index 1 are physically linked to the target segment in the final library molecule; their code-to-sample assignments and sequencing-read orientations are not specified.
The physical readout carrier is amplified target-containing DNA rather than the original RNA.
Cluster generation is the named downstream interface; neither cluster generation nor sequencing is drawn as a performed step.

operations.information_effect: Carries RNA target-sequence information into the cDNA template; no claim of quantitative conversion efficiency is established.

operations.label: Hybridization
operations.description: Bind the two custom oligos to flanking regions of the same cDNA target, producing a gapped, target-associated complex with outward oligo tails.
operations.mechanism: Hybridization places the pink and green oligo arms on the cDNA, leaving a visible interval between them.
operations.information_effect: Associates the oligo pair with the target region through the cDNA template; the diagram supplies no measurement of off-target binding or specificity.

evidence.locator: Hybridization: separated pink and green arms lie along the cDNA on opposite sides of its yellow target segment; DLSO retains the 5′ P label

operations.label: Extension-Ligation
operations.description: Fill the interval between the hybridized oligos and join them into one continuous pink/yellow/green target-spanning DNA strand, still drawn paired to the cDNA template.
operations.mechanism: The new upper yellow segment is interpreted as cDNA-templated extension joining the oligo arms by ligation at the depicted 5′-phosphorylated DLSO interface. The enzymes are not named.
operations.information_effect: Places a target-derived DNA segment between the oligo-derived flanks, creating the selected target-containing amplification substrate.

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: Denature the target-templated product and amplify it using the depicted adapter/index-bearing primers, yielding the terminal indexed DNA duplex ready for cluster generation. The intermediate strands and final duplex are retained within this combined source operation.
operations.mechanism: The denaturation/amplification caption, separated strands, primer tails and final duplex jointly depict strand separation and primer-mediated amplification; exact cycling and reaction components are unshown.
operations.information_effect: Retains the selected target segment while incorporating the P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 terminal structures into the same DNA library molecule. This supplies a target-associated carrier for the named RNA-expression assay; actual expression quantification is downstream and is not depicted. The diagram does not establish exact transcript counts, normalization, conversion/amplification efficiency or transcript-wide coverage.
